proposals.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, insulating phosphate that is chemically compatible with the sulfide electrolyte and has good oxidative stability, making it a standard protective coating for LiCoO2.
LiTaO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating oxide with a high-valent d0 Ta5+ that should resist oxidation at 4 V vs Li and limit cathode-electrolyte interdiffusion.
Li2ZrO3 is a stable, wide-gap lithium zirconate with d0 Zr4+; it is expected to be electrochemically inert over 4 V and chemically tolerant of both LiCoO2 and the sulfide.
Li3NbO4 is a lithium-rich, d0 Nb5+ oxide with a wide band gap; its high Li content should give good Li-ion compatibility and a low interfacial reaction driving force.
Li3TaO4 is a lithium-rich d0 Ta oxide with a wide gap, offering electronic insulation and oxidative stability similar to LiTaO3 but with a different Li/Ta ratio.
Li4SiO4 is a wide-gap, Li-rich orthosilicate with low redox activity; its basic oxide framework may be thermodynamically compatible with the sulfide and low-voltage contacts.
LiBO2 is a light, wide-gap lithium borate with no reducible transition metal, providing an insulating coating that should be oxidation-stable at 4 V.
LiF is a very wide-gap, electrochemically stable insulator with low reactivity toward both oxide cathodes and sulfide electrolytes, so it should give a low interfacial penalty.
Li2ZrF6 is a fluoride with a wide gap and high anodic stability; fluoride coatings resist oxidation at 4 V and may form a passivating interphase with the sulfide.
Li6Zr2O7 is a Li-rich zirconate with d0 Zr4+ and a wide gap; its high Li content could limit Li-depletion or space-charge effects at the interface.
